items.answer: Computer graphics addresses computer-generated images from synthetic models, and the software that helps a developer build a virtual reality (VR) experience should support computer-graphics operations.

A graphic display screen generally has a grid of picture elements, or pixels; when these pixels are activated, or excited, by an electrical or electromechanical means, they emit light with specific intensities that the viewer perceives as a colored image on the screen.
A generic graphics system has a host computer and a display, with three major components in between: a display controller, video memory, and a video controller.

In a raster scan system, the frame buffer is the video memory component that stores the intensity values for all pixels in the grid, and it contains one memory location for each pixel that stores the intensity as a bit string of 0s and 1s.

questions.question: Which part of the display controller computes the color values stored in the frame buffer?
options: The display processor
The frame buffer
The video controller
The display controller
questions.explanation: The color values stored in the frame buffer are computed by the display processor, which is part of the display controller.

questions.question: What is the graphics pipeline described as?
options: The set of distinct stages in which the color values stored in the frame buffer are computed
The frame buffer that stores the computed color values
The display controller that contains the display processor
The display processor that is part of the display controller
questions.explanation: The graphics pipeline is the set of the distinct stages in which the color values stored in the frame buffer are computed.

data.text: The display processor, which is part of the display controller, computes the color values stored in the frame buffer in distinct stages. The graphics pipeline is the set of these distinct stages in which the color values are computed.
points: The display processor computes color values in the frame buffer in distinct stages.
The graphics pipeline is the set of these distinct stages.

questions.question: Which stage of the 3D graphics pipeline transforms objects from their local coordinate systems to the common world coordinate system?
options: Object representation
Modeling transformation
Lighting
Scan conversion
questions.explanation: The second stage, modeling transformation, transforms objects from their local coordinate systems to the world coordinate system to construct the scene.

questions.question: What does the lighting stage of the 3D graphics pipeline do?
options: Maps the scene from world coordinates to view coordinates
Converts continuous device coordinates into integer pixel coordinates
Defines objects in local coordinates
Assigns color to the scene in world coordinates
questions.explanation: Lighting assigns color to the constructed scene in the world coordinate system, making its three-dimensional nature more perceptible.

questions.question: Which sub-stage of the viewing pipeline maps the 2D view coordinate system to the device coordinate system?
options: Window-to-viewport transformation
Viewing transformation
Projection transformation
Hidden surface removal
questions.explanation: Within the viewing pipeline, window-to-viewport transformation maps the 2D view coordinate system to the device coordinate system.

questions.question: Scan conversion changes a continuous coordinate description into integer pixel coordinates. In which coordinate system is that continuous description given?
options: Device coordinate system
Local coordinate system
Three-dimensional view coordinate system
World coordinate system
questions.explanation: Scan conversion transforms the continuous device coordinate system description, where coordinates can be real numbers, into the discrete pixel-grid or screen coordinate system.

data.text: The 3D graphics pipeline is a stage-wise process that computes pixel intensity values to drive the display. It transforms objects through stages like object representation, modeling transformation, and lighting, then uses a viewing pipeline to map the scene from the world coordinate system to the device coordinate system. Finally, scan conversion transforms the continuous device coordinate system into a discrete pixel-grid or screen coordinate system using six different coordinate systems.
points: The 3D graphics pipeline is a stage-wise process that computes pixel intensity values to drive the display.
The pipeline moves objects through stages like object representation, modeling transformation, and lighting.
The viewing pipeline maps the scene from the world coordinate system to the device coordinate system.
Scan conversion transforms the continuous device coordinate system into a discrete pixel-grid or screen coordinate system.
The process uses six coordinate systems to transform an object definition into a pixel-level scene description.

questions.question: What trade-off is central to 3D object representation?
options: Balancing efficient pipeline processing with pixel-grid resolution
Balancing realistic object detail with efficient pipeline processing
Balancing realistic object detail with lighting color accuracy
Balancing simplistic geometric approximations with efficient pipeline processing
questions.explanation: The objective is to represent objects of varied shapes and sizes with intricate details realistically while keeping later graphics pipeline operations efficient in space and time.

questions.question: Why can a more complex 3D object representation hurt rendering performance?
options: It makes the calculation of pixel intensities independent of the representation
It makes the calculation of pixel intensities more complex
It makes the calculation of pixel intensities occur before object representation
It makes the calculation of pixel intensities use a fixed number of operations
questions.explanation: Pixel-intensity computation depends on object representation, and more complex representations require more complex calculations, which can cause lags or need expensive hardware.

questions.question: Why is a single 3D object representation technique not sufficient by itself?
options: Because the appropriate technique must be chosen for a particular problem
Because every technique is sufficient for every problem
Because the technique must be chosen only for the lighting stage
Because the technique must be chosen only for the display hardware
questions.explanation: Different 3D object representation techniques are available, so the appropriate one must be selected for the problem at hand.

questions.question: Which options are the broad categories of 3D object representation?
options: Point sample rendering, mesh representation, and octree method
Octree method, binary space partitioning method, and constructive solid geometry method
Point sample rendering, boundary representation, and space partitioning based representation
Mesh representation, parametric representation, and implicit representation
questions.explanation: The broad categories are point sample rendering, boundary representation, and space partitioning based representation.

data.text: 3D object representation must balance realistic detail with computational efficiency because complex representations lead to more complex calculations that can cause lags. Since a single technique is not sufficient for every problem, the appropriate technique must be chosen for a particular problem. These techniques are grouped into broad categories such as point sample rendering, boundary representation, and space partitioning based representation.
points: 3D object representation must balance realistic detail with computational efficiency.
Complex representations lead to more complex calculations that can cause lags or require expensive hardware.
The appropriate representation technique must be chosen for a particular problem.
Broad categories of representation techniques include point sample rendering, boundary representation, and space partitioning based representation.

questions.question: Which set names the broad object-representation categories?
options: Point sample rendering, boundary representation, and implicit representation
Point sample rendering, boundary representation, and space partitioning-based representation
Point sample rendering, mesh representation, and spline representation
Mesh representation, parametric representation, and implicit representation
questions.explanation: The broad representation categories are point sample rendering, boundary representation, and space partitioning-based representation.

questions.question: How does point-sample rendering create a synthetic image?
options: It processes captured real-world points, each carrying attributes, and maps them to pixels.
It partitions the scene into spatial regions, then renders only the visible regions.
It defines synthetic objects with polygonal surfaces, then renders the connected mesh.
It computes pixel intensities from implicit surface equations instead of captured points.
questions.explanation: In point-sample rendering, real-world scene information is captured as points with attributes and then processed or mapped to pixels to generate an image, relying on real-world information rather than synthetically defining objects.

questions.question: What distinguishes boundary representation from other object representations?
options: Objects are represented directly by the pixel intensities stored in a frame buffer.
Objects are represented by dividing the scene into hierarchical spatial regions.
Objects are represented by the surfaces that define their boundary, which may be polygonal or curved.
Objects are represented as isolated raw data points that carry scene attributes.
questions.explanation: Boundary representation represents objects by the surfaces that define the object's boundary, and those surfaces can be polygonal or curved.

questions.question: What is the role of mesh representation in a rendered computer-graphics scene?
options: It is the only form used to store raw points captured by range scanners.
It is the basic object form, made of connected polygons, to which other representations are converted before rendering.
It is a partition of space used to skip invisible objects before pixel calculation.
It is a higher-level curve representation that stores spline pieces for curved surfaces.
questions.explanation: Mesh representation assumes polygonal surfaces connected into a mesh, and it is the most basic form for objects in a rendered scene; other representations are converted to mesh before rendering.

questions.question: What trade-off is involved when using a greater number of polygons in a mesh?
options: Lower storage requirements with fewer surface details.
Better surface approximation with a more complex vertex list that is harder to construct.
Simpler reconstruction with fewer boundary surfaces.
Faster pixel mapping with less realistic object detail.
questions.explanation: In mesh representation, more polygons give a better approximation of the surfaces but make the vertex list more complex and harder to construct.

data.text: Object representation categories include point sample rendering, boundary representation, and space partitioning-based representation. Point sample rendering maps real-world sensor data to pixels, while boundary representation defines objects by their surfaces. Mesh representation approximates these surfaces with polygons, requiring a trade-off between quality and complexity, and all other representations are converted to mesh before rendering.
points: Broad representation categories include point sample rendering, boundary representation, and space partitioning-based representation.
Point sample rendering captures real-world information as raw data points and maps them to pixels to generate synthetic images.
Boundary representation defines objects by their surfaces, which can be polygonal or curved.
Mesh representation approximates surfaces with polygons, requiring a trade-off between approximation quality and complexity.
All other representations are converted to a mesh representation before the objects are rendered.

questions.question: What type of object representation is spline representation?
options: A point sample rendering technique
A higher-level parametric boundary representation
A basic mesh boundary representation
A space partitioning tree method
questions.explanation: Spline representation falls under parametric representation and is a higher-level boundary representation. Mesh is the most basic boundary representation, while higher-level forms can be implicit or parametric.

questions.question: Why would a scene designer choose spline representation for curved surfaces?
options: To capture real-world points using range scanners
To create quality rendered scenes for complex artificial surfaces
To partition object space into disjoint regions
To represent objects by connected polygonal triangles
questions.explanation: Spline representation is typically used by developers or designers to construct quality rendered scenes and to represent complex artificial surfaces that cannot be represented by simple polygons or simple polynomial equations.

questions.question: How is a complete curve represented in a spline?
options: As connected triangles forming a mesh
As several lower-degree polynomial pieces, each called a blending or basis function
As a list of raw points from sensors
As one higher-degree polynomial covering the entire curve
questions.explanation: In spline representation, a complete curve is made of several lower-degree polynomial pieces rather than one higher-degree polynomial, and each piece is a blending function or basis function.

questions.question: What is the main computational advantage of using lower-degree pieces in a spline?
options: It captures real-world points directly from sensors
It partitions the object's volume into non-overlapping regions
Point computation on each curve segment is simpler and less time-consuming
It reduces the number of polygons in a mesh
questions.explanation: Computing points on a higher-degree polynomial becomes more time-consuming, while spline pieces use simpler lower-degree polynomials to compute points on their curve segments.

questions.question: What must be true about the polynomial pieces in a spline curve?
options: They must divide the scene into disjoint spatial regions
They must be stored as a complete vertex and edge list
They must join smoothly and satisfy required geometric and other properties
They must each be a single high-degree polynomial
questions.explanation: The polynomial pieces that make up a complete spline curve must join smoothly, and each piece must satisfy certain geometric and other properties.

data.text: Spline representation is a higher-level boundary representation for curved surfaces that falls under parametric representation. It is typically preferred for constructing quality scenes and representing complex surfaces that cannot be represented by simple polygons or simple polynomial equations. In spline representation, a complete curve consists of several lower-degree polynomial pieces that must join smoothly and satisfy certain properties, avoiding the more time-consuming computation of a single higher-degree complex polynomial.
points: Spline representation is a higher-level boundary representation for curved surfaces that falls under parametric representation.
It is typically preferred for constructing quality scenes and representing complex surfaces that cannot be represented by simple polygons or simple polynomial equations.
Spline representation uses several lower-degree polynomial pieces instead of a single higher-degree complex polynomial, which is more time-consuming to compute.
These pieces, which are most commonly third-order polynomials, must join smoothly and satisfy certain geometric and other properties.

questions.question: In a space partitioning representation, how is an object represented?
options: By dividing the 3D space it occupies into disjoint, non-overlapping regions and representing the occupied regions
By describing the object as self-repeating structures that repeat in larger parts
By storing only the object surface as a set of triangular meshes for the graphics pipeline
By collecting raw data points from the real-world scene and mapping those points to pixels
questions.explanation: Space partitioning representation divides the 3D space occupied by an object into disjoint, non-overlapping regions, so the object is represented by the occupied regions.

questions.question: What is a space partitioning tree?
options: A set of disjoint, non-overlapping regions used directly to represent an object
A non-hierarchical collection of raw data points captured from a real-world scene
A skeletal model that captures a complex character's appearance and motion behavior
A hierarchical, tree-like structure used to create a space partitioning representation
questions.explanation: A space partitioning tree is a hierarchical, tree-like structure that represents the space occupied by an object and is used to create a space partitioning representation.

questions.question: When are specialized sophisticated representation techniques often required?
options: For basic surfaces that can be represented by simple polygons or polynomial equations
For curves that are constructed from lower-degree polynomial pieces that join smoothly
For simple scenes that can be rendered from a set of raw captured data points
For application-specific or very complex photorealistic objects where broader boundary or space partitioning categories are insufficient
questions.explanation: Specialized sophisticated representation techniques are often needed for application-specific or very complex photorealistic objects rather than the broader boundary or space partitioning categories.

questions.question: Which specialized representation method is suited to self-repeating structures such as a leaf?
options: Space partitioning representation
Skeletal model representation
Fractal representation
Particle system representation
questions.explanation: Fractal representation is the specialized method for self-repeating structures, such as a leaf whose individual parts repeat in the larger part.

questions.question: Which specialized representation method relies on simulating physical properties for objects such as a waterfall?
options: Skeletal model representation
Point sample rendering
Particle system representation
Fractal representation
questions.explanation: Particle system representation is the specialized method for objects such as a waterfall that relies on the simulation of physical properties.

data.text: Space partitioning representation divides an object's 3D space into several disjoint, non-overlapping regions, which can be organized into a hierarchical space partitioning tree. Examples include octree, binary space partitioning, and constructive solid geometric methods. For complex photorealistic objects, specialized techniques such as fractal representations, particle systems, and skeletal models are often required.
points: Space partitioning representation divides an object's 3D space into several disjoint, non-overlapping regions.
These regions are organized into a hierarchical, tree-like structure called a space partitioning tree.
Examples of space partitioning include octree, binary space partitioning, and constructive solid geometric methods.
Specialized sophisticated representation techniques are often required for complex photorealistic objects.
Specific specialized techniques include fractal representations, particle systems, and skeletal models.

questions.question: Which statement describes the pipeline stages in an implementation of a three-dimensional graphics pipeline?
options: Only the last pipeline stage is present.
Only the scan-conversion pipeline stage is present.
Only the first pipeline stage is present.
All pipeline stages are present.
questions.explanation: In an implementation of the 3D graphics pipeline, all pipeline stages are present.

questions.question: In implementing a three-dimensional graphics pipeline, what is more important than the sequence of the stages?
options: The stage-wise display order
The stages themselves
The order of the sub-stages
The sequence itself
questions.explanation: The stages are more important than their sequence, and the implementation order may differ from the stage-wise sequence used to show computations.

data.text: In an implementation of the 3D graphics pipeline, all pipeline stages are present. The order of these stages and sub-stages may differ from the sequence used to show how the computations occur because the stages are more important than their sequence.
points: All pipeline stages are present in a 3D graphics implementation.
The order of stages may vary because their importance is greater than their sequence.

questions.question: How do the coordinate systems in the three-dimensional graphics pipeline connect object definitions to the final pixel-level description?
questions.reference_answer: The pipeline first defines objects in their local coordinate systems, then modeling transformation places them into the common world coordinate system to construct the scene. The viewing pipeline maps the scene from the world coordinate system through the three-dimensional and two-dimensional view coordinate systems to the device coordinate system. Finally, scan conversion changes the continuous device-coordinate description into the discrete screen coordinate system, where each pixel has integer coordinates. Together, these transformations use the local, world, three-dimensional view, two-dimensional view, device, and screen coordinate systems to turn object definitions into pixel-level scene descriptions.

questions.question: How does scan conversion prepare the scene for the frame buffer and pixels of a raster scan display?
questions.reference_answer: Scan conversion transforms the continuous device coordinate system description, whose points can have real-number coordinates, into the discrete pixel-grid or screen coordinate system, where each pixel coordinate is an integer. The three-dimensional graphics pipeline then computes and stores intensity values for these pixels in the frame buffer, which drives the display mechanism through the video controller. In a raster scan system, the frame buffer is the video memory that stores one intensity value for each pixel as a bit string of 0s and 1s.

questions.question: Why is no single three-dimensional object representation technique sufficient for all rendered scenes, and why is mesh representation especially important at the end of the pipeline?
questions.reference_answer: A single representation technique is not sufficient because different techniques are available and the appropriate one must be chosen for a particular problem. The broad categories are point sample rendering, boundary representation, and space partitioning based representation. Mesh representation is the most basic form of representation in computer graphics, and all other representations are converted to mesh representation at the end of the pipeline before objects are rendered.

questions.question: Why can spline representation make complex curves more practical to compute than representing them with a single high-degree polynomial?
questions.reference_answer: In polynomial representation, a more complex curve is represented by a higher-degree polynomial, and computing points on a higher-degree polynomial becomes more time-consuming. In spline representation, the complete curve is made of several lower-degree polynomial pieces, each called a blending function or basis function, so simpler polynomials can compute points on each curve segment. The pieces must join smoothly, and third-order polynomials are the most common form used to construct spline curves.
